key_insight: First-principles calculations identify a class of 109° domain walls in R3c NaNbO₃ with a notably low energy of 9 mJ m⁻².
engineering_relevance: The findings inform domain engineering in ferroelectric oxides, rather than demonstrating AI methods or solar-cell performance.
method: Classify eight domain-wall classes using group theory.
Perform first-principles structural relaxations for each representative class.
evidence_signal: The calculated low-energy 109° wall class is compatible with experimentally observed crystal twinning, and the study proposes an atomistic mechanism for the R3c ↔ Pbcm transition.
watch_item: The abstract does not report direct experimental validation of the calculated wall energy or proposed transition mechanism.
